routes.reason: Part II of Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions, 70 items. Accepted. The justification is delimitation, not novelty, and it holds: ST.0-5 are 'Families, heights and measures', 'Parametrizations by orbits', 'Geometry of numbers and uniformity', 'Fields and class groups', 'Selmer groups and rank bounds' and 'Beyond first moments' - fixed-degree objects ordered by height or discriminant, with no growing-degree polynomial law anywhere. A full-text search of the atlas extracts for random polynomials, random partitions and van der Waerden's conjecture returns nothing (the only 'van der Waerden' hits are to his Algebra, cited for Dedekind's theorem). The proposed id ArithmeticStatisticsPartIIRandomPolynomials is free, and the title 'Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions, Part II: random polynomials of growing degree' is an exact prefix extension of the parent's title, as PROTOCOL section 15 requires. Independent corroboration of the boundary: PAPER-SKOROBOGATOV-SOFOS-23 closes its gate G10 by keeping 'fixed-degree Schinzel averages separate from the growing-degree ArithmeticStatisticsPartIIRandomPolynomials', so a second paper worked by another agent expects this Part II to own exactly this material. The brief is unusually disciplined about what is and is not proved: it sets the small-factor cutoff at the verified c*eps*n/(log H)^9 and says in terms that the printed exponent 5 'remains E4, not a proved target'; it instructs the designer to use gamma below the optimal gamma(s) rather than Table 1's rounded values; and it names the two repairs (items 117 and 131) that the blueprint must carry. All five imported roadmaps exist under the exact titles the brief quotes.

Part II of the Tau Ceti roadmap Galois groups of polynomials, 22 items. Accepted, and this is the route I checked hardest, because PROTOCOL section 15 forbids re-planning a Tau Ceti roadmap. It is not re-planned. Upstream layer 5, 'Frobenius specialization', says of itself that it does not prove Dedekind's factorization theorem, that Number Field Arithmetic layer 3.10 owns it, that 'IsGoodPrime f p is p does not divide disc f' is 'the hypothesis of everything below', and that the edge case 'p divides f.discr, where a factor can repeat' is one where 'no theorem below applies'. Item 100 - a Galois element whose full cycle type is an M-merging of the mod-p factorization partition at an arbitrary, possibly ramified prime, M being the largest multiplicity - is exactly the case the upstream roadmap excludes, and the brief's instruction 'Do not replace this by an unramified-prime assertion' is the right one. 'Importing its layers 0, 1, 5 and 9' is accurate, not a typo: the upstream numbering runs 0-6 and then 9, and layer 9 is 'Sn as a Galois group over Q'. The id PolynomialGaloisGroupsPartIIRandomPartitions is free and the title is an exact prefix extension of 'Galois groups of polynomials'. The brief carries the E12 repair into the plan (items 108, 113, 117) and forbids the circular import back from the coefficient-law Part II.

Source route into FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.1, FF.3, FF.4, 9 items. Accepted. The three stages are 'Characters and elementary sums', 'Factorization and point counting' and 'Finite rings, sequences and codes', which is where the paper's Fp[T] harmonic analysis and its count of monic irreducibles belong. The reason draws the line in the right place: reuse the generic character orthogonality that is already built (item 119 credits mathlib AddChar.sum_eq_ite, which I opened) and supply only the residue-pairing nondegeneracy and the rational-frequency adapters, rather than a second Fourier transform. Recording BKK as a consumer locator for Rosen's Theorem 4.8 rather than as a substitute proof is correct.

Source route into SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.0, SV.1, SV.2, 6 items. Accepted. The paper needs exactly three sieve ingredients and each lands on the right stage: local densities and Bonferroni on SV.0 'Sieve data and local densities', the Brun sieve of section 8 on SV.1 'Brun and Selberg sieves', and the additive large sieve (3.5) on SV.2 'Large sieve and bilinear sums'. I searched both pinned trees: there is no large sieve and no Brun sieve at the pins, so item 56 is rightly not credited to any declaration. The insistence that the vector-polynomial local factor be explicit, and that no independence between the reductions be assumed unless the coefficient law proves it, is exactly the trap this paper sets.

Source route into ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.3, CA.6, 4 items. Accepted. CA.3 is 'Polynomial and matrix arithmetic' and CA.6 is 'Special algebraic numbers and Mahler measure', which is where Mignotte's factor-coefficient inequality and Dobrowolski's lower bound belong. The reason's boundary is right and I verified it at the pins: Mathlib's MahlerMeasure file already has the root formula, Landau's inequality and the choose-times-Mahler coefficient bound (items 66, 67, 68, 120, 121, all of which I opened), and its own doc-string notes that combining them gives the classical Mignotte bound - but not the sharper (m + 2 sqrt m + 2)^(1 + sqrt m) form that Lemma 3.4 uses, which is therefore correctly left missing. Dobrowolski is absent from both pinned trees, and item 69 now states it with the constant that is actually his (E21), not the Cantor-Straus one.

Source route into AnalyticNumberTheory AN.2, AN.5, 5 items. Accepted. AN.2 is 'Prime number theorems' and AN.5 is 'Multiplicative functions and value distribution', which own the prime counts of section 3.5 and the Mertens, divisor and totient estimates of sections 3.3 and 12. The reason's care not to confuse Dirichlet's theorem with the prime number theorem is justified by the pins: mathlib's Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_modEq gives primes in a coprime progression and is rightly credited for item 57, while the prime number theorem itself is not there - Tau Ceti has the smoothed Wiener-Ikehara asymptotic and Chebyshev-type machinery, but no pi(x) ~ x/log x - so item 55 is correctly 'planned' rather than 'library'. Mertens's estimates are absent from both trees (the single mathlib hit is the unrelated Dedekind-Mertens lemma).

Source route into ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory PM.0, 2 items. Accepted, and the reason is the most valuable part of it. PM.0 is 'Arithmetic probability spaces', and the concentration function with the Kolmogorov-Rogozin bound for sums of independent real variables belongs there as a general-purpose supplier, not as a random-polynomial-specific lemma - that is the right instinct, and it is what makes the E8 repair (the projection from complex z to a real direction) sit in the consumer rather than in the supplier. Nothing at the pins provides the inequality.

notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, for issue 1249, 23 September 2026. Verdict: accept.

SOURCE. arXiv 2007.14567v3 was re-fetched and hashes to adb1359df46f92d608009b32f45939672e08b1e3fe052587b035431e70d5d3e1, matching the recorded hash byte for byte; unlike a publisher PDF this one is not stamped per download, so the record is reproducible. 65 pages, printed page = PDF page, confirmed against the running heads on the even pages. The published Inventiones text (233 (2023), 1041-1120) is paywalled and was not seen, as the extraction states, so every verdict is about arXiv v3, which arXiv marks as the final version.

MISTAKES. All 25 recorded findings were checked at their locators and all 25 are confirmed; one more was added. Six are settled by the paper contradicting itself, and I report those as decisive: E1 (Theorem 7's statement bounds the probability that A has NO small divisor, while its own proof on the next page bounds the probability that it HAS one); E3 (Corollary 2 claims the setting of Theorems 1-5 while Theorem 6, eighteen lines above, says 'Theorems 1(a) and 3-5'); E14 (Lemma 9.2 requires C2 >= 3 and its application takes C2 = 2); E23 (the exponent -(t log t - t + 1) is printed correctly on pp. 44 and 48 and with the sign misplaced on p. 49); E25 (Lemma 3.1 assumes 100N and its proof says 3N); E9 (p. 53 uses n^(-2/5) for a term that Proposition 2.1, invoked two paragraphs earlier, bounds only by n^(-7/20)). E2 is refuted by a counterexample: with P = 1 condition (b) of Theorem 8 is vacuous, and mu_0 = delta_(-1), mu_j = delta_0 gives T^n - 1, reducible with abelian Galois group.

RECOMPUTED. Three numerical claims were redone from scratch rather than taken on trust. (i) E20 and item 132: computing gamma(s) over all 24 divisors Q > 1 of 210 and all shifts reproduces the extraction's list exactly - the printed gamma of Table 1 exceeds gamma(s_N) for N = 2, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18, 21, 22, 26, 27, 28, 33, 34, where alpha lies between 1.0000030 and 1.0000276 - and all 33 truncated gamma(s_N) values recorded in item 132 match mine to the last digit. (ii) For coefficients +-1, gamma(735) = 0.5000197007327024714749... at 60 digits, so the paper's printed gamma is gamma(735) itself, the exact boundary where alpha = 1 and where Theorem 7's factor (1 - n^(-1/10)) leaves no room; -log(1 - gamma(735)/735) = 0.00068053042086..., so the stated delta = 0.00068053 survives, but by 4.2e-10, which I have recorded. (iii) Item 47: max alpha(210) over N >= 35 is 0.992105 at N = 35, matching the certificate.

NEW FINDING. E26: in Case 1 of the proof of Lemma 12.9 (p. 63) the paper prints 'a subset U of its parts such that Sum_{u in U} = nr'/r', dropping the summand that the parallel display one line above prints correctly. Read on a rendered page image, not only in the text layer, since a dropped character is exactly what a text layer invents. Affects nothing.

ITEMS AND STATUSES. 133 items: 15 library, 3 planned, 115 missing. All 22 cited declarations were opened at the pinned commits and each says what its item claims; the sharper Mignotte bound, Dobrowolski, the prime number theorem, the large sieve, Mertens, the Brun sieve and any Luczak-Pyber statement are absent from both pinned trees, as the extraction says. My own structural checks: 133 unique ids, every missing item routed exactly once (the three planned items are also routed, to the layers that plan them), all prerequisites resolve, the prerequisite graph is acyclic, and all 40 definitions carry at least three API contracts and three tests.

CORRECTIONS MADE IN PLACE. (1) All 25 findings carry a review verdict, and E26 was added with mine. (2) verification.structural still said '112 missing items', the checkpoint's count from before items 131-133 were added; corrected to 115, with a note saying why. Nothing else changed: source, summary, items, routes, prerequisites, baseline, completionGates and coverage are byte-identical to the merged file.

ONE THING LEFT ALONE, DELIBERATELY. Item 103, the generalized Luczak-Pyber theorem, still describes itself as a gated target whose acceptance requires the large-part argument of E12, and its note still says no unconditional completed proof is asserted. The report's Repairs section, by contrast, presents E12 as repaired. I did not reconcile them, because the conservative reading is the honest one: the repair is a worker's, not the paper's, and item 103 is right to say so. A reader of item 103 should follow it to items 108, 113 and 117.
